messages:
Elan: Quick design review — compact 'Version playback' in Rollouts. Two main things: keyboard focus order is confusing, and screen reader announce for 'current version' is unreliable. Thoughts? Marta: I noticed that when you tab into the mini timeline the focus lands on the whole scrubber but VoiceOver says 'timeline, group' and doesn't say which version is selected. Tyler: yeah, role=slider for the scrubber might help for keyboard drag but SRs prefer focusable buttons per version. Maybe make each version a button with aria-pressed for the active one. Marta: buttons + aria-pressed sounds better. Also need an aria-live region that says "Selected version X — deployed on DATE" when you move focus. Asha (PM): agree. Also microcopy nit: current rollback CTA says "Rollback" — ambiguous. Suggest "Rollback to version X" and in the hover tooltip show the changes included. Elan: good call on explicit CTA. For compact mode we should show truncated changelog + a "View details" link so rollback isn't shocking. Tyler: implementation question: if we switch to per-version buttons, keyboard users need a "Skip to latest" control to jump to the newest version rather than tabbing through dozens. Add a visually-hidden link at the top: Skip to latest version. Marta: +1. Also the visual-only timeline uses small dark grey dots for commits — contrast fails with 3:1. We should use the brand accent at 3:1 min or add an outline when focused. accessibility-bot: Automated check: timeline dots contrast against #ffffff = 2.1:1 at small size. Recommend use #0057d7 (meets AA) or increase size to 10px. Elan: can we keep the tiny footprint but add focus ring and an enlarged hit target? 24px tappable target with visually-hidden hitbox. Tyler: doable. UX question: when a canary is running, we currently show allocation as a tiny pill with percent. Screen readers don't know that allocation is live. Suggest adding 'live canary, 5% traffic' into the aria-label and a live icon with aria-hidden=false if running. Marta: Also add a pause/resume affordance inline so operators can stop a canary without opening the details panel. Use a confirmation modal with accessible title and descriptive text. Asha (PM): For the confirmation modal copy: title "Pause canary?" body "Pausing stops new traffic to this version while retaining metrics. To rollback completely, use Rollback" buttons: "Pause" (destructive) and "Cancel" (primary? probably not). Need to pick patterns. Elan: button order should follow platform standard (primary = Continue action). If Pause is destructive, style it desctructive but keep it on the right. We'll pull from Design Tokens. Marta: small screen reader nit: when timeline compacts the labels hide. Ensure each compact button has aria-labelledby referencing a sr-only label that includes version id + timestamp. Tyler: OK. One more idea: keyboard users should be able to scrub with arrow keys and jump by page up/down to next major snapshot. Add key handlers and announce the delta in aria-live. Elan: perfect. Can someone sketch updated HTML roles and a small a11y checklist I can hand to eng? Tyler: I'll paste a quick snippet: ```html
Skip to latest version
``` Marta: great start. accessibility-bot: can you validate those patterns? accessibility-bot: Quick scan: pattern OK. Ensure aria-live updates are debounced (300ms) to avoid too many announcements. Also test NVDA+Chrome for role/button semantics. Asha (PM): timeline copy tweak: change "Deployed" to "Released" in the compact view — ops asked because "Deployed" reads more infra-y. Any objections? Marta: fine with me, but update product docs too. Elan: thanks all — Tyler can you make a small PR with the markup and a CSS sketch (focus ring + hit target) and I'll review? Then we can push a dev-preview to the staging console for a11y review. Tyler: on it, PR by EOD. Asha (PM): will add a validation checkpoint in the release checklist for screening with VoiceOver/NVDA. Elan: awesome. Follow-ups: Tyler -> PR; Marta -> copy update in docs; Asha -> release checklist update. Closing thread once PR is open. :thumbsup:
